chunks: Al-Faḍl ibn Shādhān narrated to us from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام.
He said: I said, “Can a woman lead women?”
He said: “No, except over the deceased, when there is no one more entitled than her. She stands in the middle with them in the row, then she pronounces the takbir and they pronounce the takbir.”
So the proper understanding of this report as well is that it indicates a form of recommendation, not obligation.

key_terms.أَوْلَى: more entitled or more deserving to take precedence
key_terms.تَؤُمُّ: leads in prayer; serves as the Imam for others
key_terms.تُكَبِّرُ: she says the takbir in the funeral prayer
key_terms.ٱلصَّفِّ: the row in which the worshippers stand
key_terms.ٱلنِّسَاءَ: the women being led in prayer
key_terms.ٱلِٱسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation; an act considered preferable rather than required
key_terms.ٱلْمَرْأَةُ: the woman; the subject of the legal ruling
key_terms.ٱلْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person over whom the funeral prayer is performed

ai.seo_question: Can a woman lead other women in prayer according to this hadith from al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on a woman leading other women, stating that she does not lead them except in the salat over the deceased when no one more entitled is present. In that case, she stands in the middle of the row with them and pronounces the takbir with them. The final statement clarifies that the ruling here is understood as recommendation rather than obligation.
